A1.justification: Both readable, 21-page PDFs describe the same work and include the main paper, references, and supplementary Sections 6–7. Text and visual comparison establish that pages 5–21 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, classification, dense-prediction, modality-transfer, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the supplementary normals-estimation and multiview-correspondence evaluations.

M1.justification: The teacher-student architecture, partially frozen backbone, colorization and mixup pipeline, and alignment-plus-anchoring objectives are unchanged. The abstract's replacement of 'train' with 'fine-tune' describes the procedure already documented in v1.

E1.justification: The six-dataset training mixture in Table 7 and all evaluation datasets, tasks, and modality-transfer scenarios remain unchanged, including the supplementary evaluations.

E2.justification: DINOv2 remains the comparator in the corresponding main and supplementary experiments. The frozen-TIPS comparison in Figure 9 is also unchanged; no experiment adds or removes a comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and 6 retain the same sampling, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, decoder configurations, and zero-shot testing procedures. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The anchoring-weight and mixup analyses, alternative-teacher and adapter ablations, frozen-block sweep, diagnostic metrics, and qualitative cases are unchanged in Section 4.4 and Appendix 7.

E5.justification: The same point-estimate tables and plots remain. Neither version adds or changes seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same ScanNet GAP R@1 values in both versions: 46.1% for Omnivorous and 4.6% for DINOv2. Supplementary result tables and figures are also identical.

T1.justification: The feature and modality-mixture definitions, loss equations (1)–(4), and Appendix 6 colorization mathematics are unchanged. Equation reflow introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The claims of cross-modal alignment, semantic preservation, and transfer to unseen modalities remain. The abstract's 'post-training' terminology and 'more consistent embeddings' wording refine the description without redefining the contribution or its scope.

C2.justification: The alignment–discernibility trade-off, explanations of transfer gains and regressions, supplementary interpretations, and uncertainty about high-resolution fine-tuning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds a statement that model weights are available and a repository link, absent from v1. Implementation details remain unchanged. This establishes added access information, while the linked resources themselves cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions and cited works are unchanged. Replacing 'novel framework' with 'post-training framework' in the abstract matches the post-hoc alignment positioning already present in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract receives limited terminology and phrasing edits, including 'visual modalities,' 'post-training,' and 'fine-tune,' plus the model-weight statement. The remaining narrative and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised abstract causes local text and equation reflow across pages 1–4, including movement of modality-mixture definitions onto page 4. Figures, tables, and captions are unchanged; pages 5–21 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a previously absent model-weight access pointer and describes the existing post-training procedure more precisely in the abstract. These modest improvements to access information and clarity leave the scientific evidence and appendices unchanged; actual resource availability is not established by the local PDFs.
